book: Sheep!
A sheep has a soft, woolly coat.
Every year the wool is cut off, and it grows back. Wool is made into warm sweaters and blankets.
Sheep know their shepherd’s voice and follow it. Jesus said He is the Good Shepherd, and His sheep know His voice.
A sheep lives on land. It eats plants. A baby sheep is called a lamb.
A sheep says baa!
Cat!
A cat purrs when it is happy.
A cat’s whiskers are as wide as its body, so it can tell if it fits through a gap.
Cats can see in very dim light, six times better than we can, which is why they love to prowl at night.
A cat lives on land. It eats other animals. A baby cat is called a kitten.
A cat says meow!

A dog wags its tail when it is glad to see you.
A dog’s nose can smell thousands of times better than yours.
Dogs can learn hundreds of words, and some dogs help people who cannot see to find their way.
A dog lives on land. It eats plants and animals. A baby dog is called a puppy.
A dog says woof!

A pig has a curly tail and a flat nose called a snout.
Pigs roll in mud to keep cool, because they cannot sweat.
Pigs are very clever, about as clever as a dog, and they can learn their own names.
A pig lives on land. It eats plants and animals. A baby pig is called a piglet.
A pig says oink!

A hen is a mother chicken. She lays eggs.
A hen lays about one egg a day, and she sits on her eggs to keep them warm.
A chick peeps inside its egg before it hatches, and the hen clucks back to it.
A hen lives on land. It eats plants and animals. A baby hen is called a chick.
A hen says cluck!
Chick!
A chick is a baby chicken. It is soft and yellow.
A chick pecks its way out of its egg with a tiny egg tooth on its beak.
A chick can walk and peck for food on the very day it hatches, but it stays close to its mother for warmth.
A chick lives on land. It eats plants and animals. A baby chick is called a chick.
A chick says peep!

A cow eats grass and gives us milk.
A cow chews its food, swallows it, then brings it back up to chew again. That is called chewing the cud.
A cow’s stomach has four parts, which help it turn tough grass into milk. Butter, cheese and yogurt all come from milk.
A cow lives on land. It eats plants. A baby cow is called a calf.
A cow says moo!

A goat lives on land. It eats plants. A baby goat is called a kid.

A duck swims on the pond and says quack.
A duck’s feathers are oily, so water rolls right off and it never gets soaked.
Ducklings can swim on their first day, and they follow their mother in a line wherever she goes.
A duck lives on land. It eats plants and animals. A baby duck is called a duckling.
A duck says quack!
Mouse!
A mouse is tiny. It has a long tail and big ears.
A mouse can squeeze through a hole as small as a coin.
A mouse’s whiskers feel its way in the dark, and its teeth never stop growing, so it has to keep nibbling.
A mouse lives on land. It eats plants and animals. A baby mouse is called a pup.
A mouse says squeak!
Rat!
A rat is like a big mouse, with a long tail.
Rats are very clever and can learn tricks, like running through a maze.
Rats wash themselves many times a day, and they laugh with tiny squeaks when they play.
A rat lives on land. It eats plants and animals. A baby rat is called a pup.
A rat says squeak!
Bunny!
A bunny hops. It has long ears and a fluffy tail.
A bunny’s big ears can turn to hear a sound from any direction.
A rabbit’s eyes are on the sides of its head, so it can see almost all the way around without turning.
A bunny lives on land. It eats plants. A baby bunny is called a kit.
A bunny says a soft thump!
Frog!
A frog hops and says ribbit.
A baby frog is a tadpole. It has a tail and no legs, and it swims like a fish.
A tadpole grows legs, loses its tail and climbs out of the water as a frog. A frog drinks through its skin.
A frog lives on land. It eats other animals. A baby frog is called a tadpole.
A frog says ribbit!
Caterpillar!
A caterpillar crawls and eats leaves.
A caterpillar eats and eats, then wraps itself up. Inside, it turns into a butterfly.
A caterpillar has twelve tiny eyes, but it can barely see. It finds leaves by feel and smell.
A caterpillar lives on land. It eats plants. A baby caterpillar is called a caterpillar.
A caterpillar makes no sound at all.
Ant!
An ant is tiny and very strong.
An ant can carry something many times heavier than itself.
Ants live together in a colony with one queen, and they talk by touching feelers and leaving smells to follow.
A ant lives on land. It eats plants and animals. A baby ant is called a larva.
A ant makes no sound at all.
Ladybug!
A ladybug is red with black spots.
A ladybug eats tiny bugs that hurt plants, so gardeners love it.
A ladybug’s bright red color warns birds that it tastes bad. It hides its wings under its spotted shell.
A ladybug lives in the sky. It eats other animals. A baby ladybug is called a larva.
A ladybug makes no sound at all.
Bee!
A bee buzzes from flower to flower.
Bees make honey from the sweet nectar they find in flowers.
A bee dances to tell the other bees where the best flowers are. Bees also help fruit and seeds grow.
A bee lives in the sky. It eats plants. A baby bee is called a larva.
A bee says buzz!
Butterfly!
A butterfly has four pretty wings.
A butterfly was once a caterpillar.
A butterfly tastes with its feet! It drinks nectar from flowers through a tube like a straw.
A butterfly lives in the sky. It eats plants. A baby butterfly is called a caterpillar.
A butterfly makes no sound at all.
Snake!
A snake has no legs. It slides along the ground.
A snake smells with its tongue, flicking it in and out.
As a snake grows, its skin gets too tight, so it wriggles out of the old skin in one piece.
A snake lives on land. It eats other animals. A baby snake is called a hatchling.
A snake says hiss!
Bat!
A bat flies at night and sleeps in the day.
A bat sleeps hanging upside down by its feet.
A bat is the only mammal that can fly. In the dark it makes tiny squeaks and listens to the echoes to find its way.
A bat lives in the sky. It eats plants and animals. A baby bat is called a pup.
A bat says squeak!
Owl!
An owl has big round eyes and says hoot.
An owl hunts at night and can see in the dark.
An owl can turn its head almost all the way around, and its soft feathers let it fly without a sound.
A owl lives in the sky. It eats other animals. A baby owl is called a owlet.
A owl says hoot!
Lion!
A lion is a big cat. It roars!
Lions live together in a family called a pride.
A lion’s roar is so loud it can be heard five miles away. Daniel spent a whole night with lions, and God kept him safe.
A lion lives on land. It eats other animals. A baby lion is called a cub.
A lion says roar!
Elephant!
An elephant is the biggest animal on land.
An elephant uses its long trunk to drink, to smell and to pick up food.
An elephant flaps its big ears to keep cool, and it can hear sounds from miles away through its feet.
A elephant lives on land. It eats plants. A baby elephant is called a calf.
A elephant says trumpet!
Giraffe!
A giraffe is the tallest animal of all.
A giraffe’s neck is so long it can eat leaves from the tops of trees.
A giraffe’s tongue is as long as your arm and dark purple, and it only needs a short nap each day.
A giraffe lives on land. It eats plants. A baby giraffe is called a calf.
A giraffe says a quiet hum!
Zebra!
A zebra has black and white stripes.
No two zebras have the same stripes, just like no two people have the same fingerprints.
Zebras live in big herds, and their stripes make it hard for a lion to pick just one out of the crowd.
A zebra lives on land. It eats plants. A baby zebra is called a foal.
A zebra says bray!
Monkey!
A monkey swings from tree to tree.
Many monkeys can hang from a branch by their tail.
Monkeys live in groups and groom each other’s fur to show they are friends.
A monkey lives on land. It eats plants and animals. A baby monkey is called a baby.
A monkey says chatter!
Gorilla!
A gorilla is big and strong, with long arms.
Gorillas eat leaves and fruit all day long.
A father gorilla has silver hair on his back, so he is called a silverback. He keeps his family safe.
A gorilla lives on land. It eats plants. A baby gorilla is called a baby.
A gorilla says grunt!
Bear!
A bear is big and furry.
A bear sleeps for most of the winter in a cozy den.
Bears love honey and berries. David fought off a bear to protect his sheep, long before he was king.
A bear lives on land. It eats plants and animals. A baby bear is called a cub.
A bear says growl!
Fox!
A fox has red fur and a bushy tail.
A fox sleeps curled up with its fluffy tail over its nose.
A fox can hear a mouse squeak from far away, even under the snow, and pounce right on it.
A fox lives on land. It eats plants and animals. A baby fox is called a kit.
A fox says yip!
Penguin!
A penguin is a bird that cannot fly.
A penguin cannot fly, but it swims very fast, flapping its wings underwater.
A penguin father keeps the egg warm on top of his feet through the long, cold winter.
A penguin lives on land. It eats other animals. A baby penguin is called a chick.
A penguin says squawk!
Eagle!
An eagle is a big bird with huge wings.
An eagle can see a rabbit from high, high up in the sky.
An eagle’s eyes are much sharper than ours, and it builds its nest at the top of a tall tree or a cliff.
A eagle lives in the sky. It eats other animals. A baby eagle is called a eaglet.
A eagle says screech!
Bird!
A bird has feathers and wings.
A bird builds a nest for its eggs, and sings to say good morning.
God used birds to feed Elijah: ravens brought him bread and meat every morning and evening.
A bird lives in the sky. It eats plants and animals. A baby bird is called a chick.
A bird says tweet!
Dove!
A dove is a gentle white bird. It says coo.
Noah sent a dove out from the ark, and it came back with an olive leaf.
The olive leaf told Noah the water was going down. A dove is a sign of peace to this day.
A dove lives in the sky. It eats plants. A baby dove is called a squab.
A dove says coo!
Fish!
A fish swims. It breathes under the water.
A fish breathes with gills, and most fish are covered in shiny scales.
Fish never close their eyes, because they have no eyelids. Jesus fed thousands of people with two small fish.
A fish lives in the sea. It eats plants and animals. A baby fish is called a fry.
A fish makes no sound at all.
Rainbow fish!
A rainbow fish has bright colors.
Bright colors help a fish hide among the colorful coral.
Coral reefs are like busy underwater cities, home to thousands of kinds of fish.
A rainbow fish lives in the sea. It eats plants and animals. A baby rainbow fish is called a fry.
A rainbow fish makes no sound at all.
Dolphin!
A dolphin jumps and plays in the sea.
A dolphin is not a fish. It breathes air through a hole on top of its head.
Dolphins talk with clicks and whistles, and each one has its own name-whistle.
A dolphin lives in the sea. It eats other animals. A baby dolphin is called a calf.
A dolphin says click and whistle!
Octopus!
An octopus has eight arms.
An octopus can change color to hide, and squirt ink to get away.
An octopus has three hearts and blue blood, and it can squeeze through any gap bigger than its eye.
A octopus lives in the sea. It eats other animals. A baby octopus is called a larva.
A octopus makes no sound at all.
Whale!
A whale is the biggest animal in the sea.
A whale is not a fish. It breathes air through a blowhole on its back.
The blue whale is the biggest animal that has ever lived, as long as three buses, and it sings songs across the ocean.
A whale lives in the sea. It eats other animals. A baby whale is called a calf.
A whale says a song!
Big fish!
A big fish swallowed Jonah. God kept him safe inside.
The biggest fish alive today is the whale shark. It is as long as a bus, and it is gentle.
The Bible says a great fish swallowed Jonah. A whale shark only eats tiny things, so it was a special fish God sent.
A big fish lives in the sea. It eats other animals. A baby big fish is called a fry.
A big fish makes no sound at all.
Camel!
A camel has a hump and lives in the desert.
A camel’s hump is full of fat, not water, so it can go a long time without eating.
A camel can close its nose to keep out blowing sand, and it has long eyelashes to protect its eyes.
A camel lives on land. It eats plants. A baby camel is called a calf.
A camel says grunt!
Donkey!
A donkey has long ears and says hee-haw.
A donkey is small but strong, and it can carry heavy loads a long way.
Jesus rode into Jerusalem on a donkey, while the crowd waved palm branches and shouted hosanna.
A donkey lives on land. It eats plants. A baby donkey is called a foal.
A donkey says hee-haw!
Horse!
A horse runs fast and says neigh.
A horse can sleep standing up.
A baby horse can stand and run just hours after it is born, and a horse’s hooves grow like our fingernails.
A horse lives on land. It eats plants. A baby horse is called a foal.
A horse says neigh!
Quail!
A quail is a small, round bird.
Quail make their nests on the ground, hidden in the grass.
When God’s people were hungry in the desert, He sent quail in the evening and manna in the morning.
A quail lives on land. It eats plants and animals. A baby quail is called a chick.
A quail says a whistle!
Where does each animal live? On the land, in the sea, or up in the sky?
That's right, the land!
That's right, the sea!
That's right, the sky!

That's right, bigger than you!
That's right, smaller than you!

think: Think about it! Why did Noah build the big boat? Because God told him to, to go fishing, or to win a race?
Noah trusted God, so he obeyed, even before the rain came. Trusting God means doing what He says.
Think about it! Why did God put a rainbow in the sky? To paint the clouds, to show His promise, or for the birds to sit on?
For the birds to sit on!
The rainbow is God's promise that He would never flood the whole earth again. God always keeps His promises.
Think about it! How do you think God felt when He looked at what He made? Scared, cross, or happy?
God saw that everything He made was good. He was glad, and He still loves the world He made.
Think about it! Why did God make you? To be His friend, to be a robot, or to sit still like a rock?
To sit still like a rock!
God made Adam and Eve to be His friends, and He made you to be His friend, too. You are wonderfully made!
Think about it! Why did God pick David to be king one day? He was the tallest, God looks at the heart, or he had a crown?
David's brothers were tall and strong, but God looks at the heart. David loved God, and that is what God saw.
Think about it! Why was David not afraid of the giant? He had a big sword, he could run fast, or he trusted God?
David knew God had helped him before, so God would help him again. God is bigger than any giant.
Think about it! Why did Jonah get on the boat? To run away from God, to catch fish, or to go to the beach?
Jonah did not want to do what God said, so he ran the other way. But no one can hide from God, and God still loved Jonah.
Think about it! Why did God give Jonah a second chance? Because the fish asked, because God loves us, or because it was his birthday?
Jonah said sorry, and God forgave him and sent him again. When we say sorry, God forgives us, too.
Think about it! Why did the boy give Jesus his lunch? He didn't like it, he was too sleepy to eat, or to share and help?
He was too sleepy to eat!
The boy only had a little, but he shared it with Jesus. When we share, Jesus can do big things with it.
Think about it! What does the story show us about Jesus? He gives us what we need, he runs very fast, or he likes to paint?
He gives us what we need!
One little lunch fed thousands, with baskets left over. Jesus cares for us and gives us what we need.
Think about it! Why did Mary and Joseph sleep where the animals sleep? They loved sheep best, there was no room anywhere else, or it was a fun camp-out?
There was no room anywhere else!
The town was full, so there was no room. God's Son was born in a humble place, for everyone, not just for kings.
Think about it! Why is Jesus God's best gift? He came in a shiny box, he is sweet like candy, or he came to rescue us?
He came in a shiny box!
Jesus is our Savior. God sent Him to rescue us, because God loves us so much.
Think about it! Why did Abraham leave his home? Because he trusted God, his house was too small, or the camels wanted a walk?
Abraham did not know where he was going, but he trusted God and went. Trusting God means going where He leads.
Think about it! Why did Sarah laugh when she heard about the baby? A clown was there, she thought she was too old, or it was a party?
She thought she was too old!
Sarah thought it was impossible. But nothing is too hard for God, and He kept His promise. Then she laughed for joy!
Think about it! Why were Joseph's brothers unkind to him? They were sleepy, they wanted to give him a gift, or they were jealous?
They wanted to give him a gift!
Jealousy made the brothers do a very wrong thing. Being jealous can make us unkind, so we can ask God for a kind heart.
Think about it! How did Joseph treat his brothers when they came to Egypt? He forgave them, he sent them away, or he laughed at them?
Joseph forgave his brothers, even after they hurt him. God turned something bad into something good.
Think about it! How did the people feel when the chariots came? Silly, scared, or sleepy?
They were scared, but Moses said, do not be afraid, God will help us. When we are scared, we can trust God, too.
Think about it! Why did everyone sing and dance after they crossed the sea? There was cake, they heard a band, or God had saved them?
God made a way through the sea and kept His people safe. When God helps us, we can thank Him with songs.
Think about it! Why did Daniel keep praying when it was against the rule? He loved God most of all, he forgot the rule, or he liked to be silly?
He loved God most of all!
Daniel loved God more than anything, even more than being safe. Praying to God was the most important thing to him.
Think about it! Why did the king not sleep that night? He was playing games, he was worried about Daniel, or he ate too much pizza?
The king loved Daniel and was worried for him. But God kept Daniel safe all night long. God is always with us.
Think about it! Why did Moses' mom put him in a basket? To give him a bath, to play boats, or to keep him safe?
Pharaoh's rule was unkind, so she hid her baby to keep him safe. And God was watching over him the whole time.
Think about it! How did the princess feel when she saw the baby? Kind and loving, cross, or silly?
The princess felt kind and loving, and she took care of him. God used the princess to keep baby Moses safe. God had a plan!
Think about it! Why did Moses help the sisters at the well? They paid him, he was kind, or to win a prize?
Moses saw that it was not kind to push them away, so he helped. God wants us to be kind, like Moses was.
Think about it! Why did God tell Moses to take off his sandals? His socks were wet, his sandals were dirty, or because God was there?
The ground was holy because God was there. When we talk to God, we remember He is great, and He is with us.
Think about it! Why did God send bread even after the people grumbled? Because He still loved them, because they shouted loudest, or because He had too much bread?
Because He had too much bread!
God heard the grumbling, but He still loved His people and fed them. God is kind to us even when we grumble.
Think about it! Why did God say to gather just enough for today? So the ants could eat, so they would trust Him every day, or so their bags would stay light?
So they would trust Him every day!
So their bags would stay light!
God wanted His people to trust Him for each new day. God gives us what we need, every single day.
Think about it! Why did Rahab hide the two men? She liked hide and seek, they brought cookies, or she believed in God?
Rahab said, I know your God is the real God. She trusted God, and God kept her family safe.
Think about it! Why did the walls fall down? God made them fall, the people pushed them, or an elephant bumped them?
The people did just what God said, and God made the walls fall. God keeps His promises, and He gives the victory.
Think about it! Why did Ruth stay with Naomi? Naomi had cake, she loved her, or she lost her way?
Ruth loved Naomi, and she chose Naomi's God, too. Real love stays close, no matter what.
Think about it! Why did Boaz tell his workers to drop extra barley? He hated sweeping, it was a game, or to be kind to Ruth?
Boaz was kind, and he helped Ruth without being asked. God takes care of us through kind people.
Think about it! How did Hannah feel after she prayed? Not sad anymore, cross, or scared?
Hannah told God what she wanted, and she felt peace. God hears us when we pray.
Think about it! Why did Samuel run to Eli? He wanted a snack, he thought Eli called him, or he loved running?
Samuel did not know God's voice yet. Eli taught him to say, Speak, Lord, I am listening. We can listen to God in the Bible.
Think about it! Why did the widow share her last bread with Elijah? She didn't like bread, the ravens told her to, or she trusted God's promise?
Elijah said God would make her flour and oil last, and she trusted God. God took care of her family every day.
Think about it! Why did Elijah pour water all over the altar? So everyone would know God did it, to put out the fire, or to wash the stones?
So everyone would know God did it!
Wet wood cannot burn, so when fire came, everyone knew it was God. The Lord is God, and He answers prayer.
Think about it! Why would Mordecai not bow down to Haman? His knees hurt, he bowed only to God, or he was asleep?
Mordecai bowed only to God. And God made Esther queen for a time just like this.
Think about it! Why did Esther pray for three days before seeing the king? It was her birthday, she was sleepy, or she was afraid and needed God's help?
She was afraid and needed God's help!
Esther was afraid, so she asked God and her friends to pray. Then she was brave. God takes care of His people.
Think about it! Why did Jesus' family go to Jerusalem? To praise God at the feast, to ride a roller coaster, or to buy new shoes?
To praise God at the feast!
The Passover feast was a time to remember how God set His people free. Jesus loved to go to God's house.
Think about it! Why was Jesus in God's house? He was hiding, he loved to learn about God, or he wanted ice cream?
He loved to learn about God!
Jesus wanted to be in His Father's house, listening and asking questions. Then He went home and obeyed Mary and Joseph.
Think about it! Why did Peter let down the nets again? He saw a fish jump, he was bored, or because Jesus said so?
Peter had worked all night and caught nothing. But he did what Jesus said. Obeying Jesus brings good things.
Think about it! Why did Peter and his friends leave their boats? To follow Jesus, to go swimming, or to go to bed?
Jesus said, come, follow Me. They left everything to go with Him. Jesus wants you to follow Him, too.
Think about it! Why was Jesus asleep in the boat? He was hiding, he was tired after a long day, or he was bored?
He was tired after a long day!
Jesus was tired after teaching all day. Jesus is God's Son, and He was a real person, too, who got tired like us.
Think about it! Why did the friends wake Jesus up? It was dinner time, they wanted a party, or they were scared?
They were scared, but Jesus was with them the whole time. When we are scared, Jesus is with us, and He takes care of us.
Think about it! Why did the shepherd go looking for just one lamb? He loved every one of them, he was cross with it, or he wanted dinner?
He loved every one of them!
The shepherd loved every sheep, even the littlest lamb. God loves every one of us like that.
Think about it! Why did the shepherd have a party? It was his birthday, he found his lost lamb, or it was raining?
The shepherd was so happy to find his lamb. When one of us comes home to God, heaven is full of joy!
Think about it! Why did the Samaritan stop? His donkey was tired, he wanted to buy something, or he felt sorry for the hurt man?
He felt sorry for the hurt man!
The priest and the helper walked by, but the Samaritan stopped because he cared. A neighbor is anyone who needs our help.
Think about it! What did Jesus want the man to learn? To be kind to everyone, to hurry past, or to buy a donkey?
Jesus said, go and do the same. God wants us to be kind to everyone, even people who are different from us.
Think about it! Why did Zacchaeus climb the tree? To pick apples, he wanted to see Jesus, or he was playing monkey?
Zacchaeus was short, but he wanted to see Jesus so much. Jesus saw him, too, and He knew his name.
Think about it! Why did Zacchaeus give the money back? A guard made him, he had too much, or Jesus' love changed his heart?
Jesus loved Zacchaeus, and that love changed his heart. Jesus loves everyone, and His love changes hearts.
Think about it! Why did the owners let the friends take the donkey? The Lord needed it, they were paid, or they were asleep?
The friends said, the Lord needs it, and the owners let it go. Jesus knew just what would happen. He is the King.
Think about it! Why did the people shout Hosanna? They were cross, to praise Jesus the King, or to call the donkey?
Hosanna is a happy shout that praises God. The people welcomed Jesus as their King, and He is our King, too.
Think about it! How did Jesus' friends feel after He died? Happy, sleepy, or very sad?
They were very sad, and they missed Him. But that was not the end of the story!
Think about it! Why were the women so happy at the garden? Jesus was alive, the flowers were pretty, or they found breakfast?
Jesus was alive! He is alive forever, and He loves you, too.
Think about it! Why did the friends wait and pray in Jerusalem? It was raining, Jesus told them to wait for the Helper, or they missed the bus?
Jesus told them to wait for the Helper!
Jesus promised to send the Holy Spirit, the Helper. They trusted Jesus and waited, just like He said.
Think about it! How did Peter become so brave? He ate his vegetables, he won a race, or the Holy Spirit filled him?
The Holy Spirit made Peter brave to tell everyone about Jesus. God's Helper is with God's family today, too.

wool!
tiny drops of water!
Did you know? Shiny things, like a gold crown, bounce light back to your eyes. Try it at home: Shine a flashlight at a mirror in a dark room. Where does the light go?

Did you know? Smooth, shiny things bounce light the way a ball bounces off a wall. A mirror is so smooth that the light bounces straight back, and you see yourself. Try it at home: Shine a flashlight at a mirror in a dark room. Where does the light go?

Did you know? Gold is a metal that never rusts or goes dull, so it stays shiny for thousands of years. That is one reason kings and queens wore it. Try it at home: Shine a flashlight at a mirror in a dark room. Where does the light go?
Why does a gold crown shine? It bounces light back to your eyes, it is on fire, or it has a light bulb inside?
it bounces light back to your eyes!
it is on fire!
it has a light bulb inside!
Did you know? You grow when you sleep, eat good food and play. Try it at home: Have a grown-up mark your height on a door frame. Check it again in a few months!

Did you know? Your bones get longer a tiny bit at a time. That is why your shoes get too small! Milk, vegetables and running around help your bones grow strong. Try it at home: Have a grown-up mark your height on a door frame. Check it again in a few months!

Did you know? You will keep growing until you are about eighteen. Your brain grows too: every time you learn something new, it builds new paths inside. Try it at home: Have a grown-up mark your height on a door frame. Check it again in a few months!
What helps you grow? Watching television all day, good food, sleep and play, or only candy?
watching television all day!
good food, sleep and play!
only candy!

Did you know? A fish breathes under water with gills, the little slits on the sides of its head. Try it at home: Watch a fish in a tank or a pond. Can you see its gills opening and closing as it breathes?

Did you know? Water has air mixed in it. The gills take the air out of the water as it flows through, so a fish never has to come up to breathe. Try it at home: Watch a fish in a tank or a pond. Can you see its gills opening and closing as it breathes?

Did you know? Fish swim in big groups called schools to stay safe. A net catches a whole school at once, which is why Peter's nets were so full. Try it at home: Watch a fish in a tank or a pond. Can you see its gills opening and closing as it breathes?
How does a fish breathe? With a nose, above the water, with gills, under the water, or it holds its breath all day?
with a nose, above the water!
with gills, under the water!
it holds its breath all day!
Did you know? Waves are made by the wind blowing across the water. Try it at home: Blow across a bowl of water. Blow softly, then hard. Watch the waves get bigger!

Did you know? The harder and longer the wind blows, the bigger the waves get. A storm has strong wind, so it makes big waves that can splash into a boat. Try it at home: Blow across a bowl of water. Blow softly, then hard. Watch the waves get bigger!

Did you know? A wave carries energy from the wind across the water, but the water itself mostly goes up and down. When the wind stops, the waves settle, though never as fast as when Jesus said, be still! Try it at home: Blow across a bowl of water. Blow softly, then hard. Watch the waves get bigger!
What makes waves on a lake? The wind blowing across the water, the fish swimming, or the moon singing?
the wind blowing across the water!
the fish swimming!
the moon singing!
Did you know? Sheep know their shepherd's voice and come when he calls. Try it at home: Close your eyes and listen. Can you tell who is talking just by their voice?

Did you know? A sheep's ears can turn to catch sounds from all around. A lamb's bleat is how it calls its mother, and the mother knows her own lamb's voice. Try it at home: Close your eyes and listen. Can you tell who is talking just by their voice?

Did you know? Sheep have eyes on the sides of their heads, so they can see almost all the way around without turning. That helps them spot danger, but they still get lost! Try it at home: Close your eyes and listen. Can you tell who is talking just by their voice?
How does a sheep know its shepherd? It smells his shoes, it reads his name, or it knows his voice?
it smells his shoes!
it reads his name!
it knows his voice!
Did you know? A bandage keeps a hurt clean so it can heal. Try it at home: Next time you get a little scrape, watch it over a few days. Can you see the new skin growing?

Did you know? Your body fixes itself! New skin grows under a scab, and the scab falls off when the new skin is ready. Try it at home: Next time you get a little scrape, watch it over a few days. Can you see the new skin growing?

Did you know? Blood has tiny helpers in it. When you get a cut, some of them make a plug to stop the bleeding, and others fight germs. Washing a cut and covering it helps them work. Try it at home: Next time you get a little scrape, watch it over a few days. Can you see the new skin growing?
Why do we cover a cut? To make it pretty, to keep it clean so it can heal, or to put it to sleep?
to make it pretty!
to keep it clean so it can heal!
to put it to sleep!
Did you know? A tree grows up tall toward the sun, with roots going down into the ground. Try it at home: Hug a tree and look up. Can you see how its branches reach for the sun?

Did you know? A tree drinks water through its roots, and its leaves use sunlight to make food. A sycamore's branches grow wide and low, which made it easy to climb. Try it at home: Hug a tree and look up. Can you see how its branches reach for the sun?

Did you know? Trees give us the air we breathe. Leaves take in the air we breathe out and give back fresh oxygen. One big tree can make enough oxygen for four people. Try it at home: Hug a tree and look up. Can you see how its branches reach for the sun?
What does a tree drink water with? Its leaves, its squirrels, or its roots?
its leaves!
its squirrels!
its roots!
Did you know? A palm tree has big leaves called fronds that grow at the very top. Try it at home: Find the biggest leaf you can outside. Wave it like a flag!
Did you know? Palm trees grow in warm places. Their leaves can be as long as a car! People waved them like flags for Jesus. Try it at home: Find the biggest leaf you can outside. Wave it like a flag!

Did you know? A palm tree does not have branches like other trees. Its trunk grows straight up, and dates, a sweet fruit, grow in bunches under the leaves. Try it at home: Find the biggest leaf you can outside. Wave it like a flag!
Where do a palm tree's leaves grow? At the very top, at the bottom, or under the ground?
at the very top!
at the bottom!
under the ground!
Did you know? The sun comes up in the morning in the east, and goes down at night in the west. Try it at home: Wake up early one morning and watch the sunrise. What colors do you see?

Did you know? The sun is not really moving up. The earth is turning, and our side slowly turns to face the sun. The sky turns pink and orange before the sun appears. Try it at home: Wake up early one morning and watch the sunrise. What colors do you see?

Did you know? Sunrise is pink and orange because the sunlight travels through a lot of air when the sun is low, and the air scatters away the blue light, leaving the warm colors. Try it at home: Wake up early one morning and watch the sunrise. What colors do you see?
Why does the sun seem to come up in the morning? The sun flies up, the earth turns to face the sun, or a balloon lifts it?
the sun flies up!
the earth turns to face the sun!
a balloon lifts it!
Did you know? Your voice is made by air from your lungs shaking two little strings in your throat. Try it at home: Put your fingers on your throat and say ahhh. Feel the buzz of your voice!

Did you know? When you talk, air from your lungs passes over your vocal cords and makes them shake. Your tongue and lips shape the shaking air into words. Try it at home: Put your fingers on your throat and say ahhh. Feel the buzz of your voice!

Did you know? People around the world speak about seven thousand different languages, but every baby is born able to learn any of them. Peter's friends spoke languages they had never learned, which was a miracle. Try it at home: Put your fingers on your throat and say ahhh. Feel the buzz of your voice!
Where does your voice come from? Your ears, your feet, or air from your lungs shaking strings in your throat?
your ears!
your feet!
air from your lungs shaking strings in your throat!
